article.title: The political economy of Kansas fiscal policy (from the comments)
article.excerpt: MR commentator Patrick L. has a go at it : OK I’ll bite. In nominal terms, between 2002 and 2012 state receipts grew 50%. Inflation in this period was 28%, and probably significantly lower for Kansas, while population growth has only been about 10% since 2000. Even the “low” 2014 receipts are $1.5 billion more in revenue from when Sebelius first took office
